expectations.text: A1 Zones marked and ordered: the document opens with a human zone whose heading or banner names its audience (a pointer line in the header does not count), and any AI-input or archive material sits last in its own labelled zone; nothing for people follows machine content

The document does not open with a human zone whose heading or banner names its audience: line 1 is the title, lines 3-10 are a metadata table, and its row ‘读者 | 研发团队全体；技术负责人张伟据此决定改进项的先后’ (line 8) is exactly the header pointer line the expectation says does not count; the first heading is ‘## 1. 摘要与待决事项’ (line 14). The raw chat does sit last (Appendix C, line 237) and nothing for people follows it, but under a plain ‘附录 C’ heading, not in a labelled archive or AI-input zone.

expectations.text: A3 Machine and archive blocks are collapsed in details blocks and plain-headed, each opening with a line that names its bin (AI input or archive) and what it supports; long material sits in a sibling file behind a pointer
expectations.evidence: stats.details_blocks = 0, so nothing is collapsed. The only raw/archive material, the chat log, is an open 28-line fenced block (lines 241-270) under ‘附录 C 原始群聊记录’ (line 237), and Appendices A and B (lines 208-235) are open tables. The Appendix C lead-in (line 239: ‘以下为故障群聊记录原文，共 28 条，未做任何修改…’) does not name a bin (archive or AI input) or say which claim it supports, and the log is not in a sibling file behind a one-line pointer.

expectations.text: B1 Reading path: within 60 lines of the title there are at least 3 links to sections, each saying what the reader gets, and a line saying who can stop where

There is no reading-path block telling the reader what each section gives them, and no line saying who can stop where (a search for such wording finds nothing; the only audience text is the ‘读者’ metadata row on line 8). check_doc.py's link-count test passes (no B1 finding), but the judged part of the rule is not met.

expectations.text: B2 Order follows understanding: the mental model comes first, terms are defined before the first section that uses them, and chronology lives in the archive (or is a compact timeline in the human zone with the raw chat log in the archive)
expectations.evidence: The structure is Summary → Impact → Timeline → Cause, i.e. chronology first. A 23-row, discovery-order timeline table (§3.2, lines 67-93) sits in the main body before the root-cause section (§4, line 95) and before the propagation diagram that is the real mental model (§4.1, lines 99-108); mechanical.json flags it as A2 ‘23-row table in the human zone’. Only §3.1 (5-row phase table) is compact. Terms are mostly defined before use (A1-A6 glossed in the decision box, † defined on line 50), but ‘A7’ is used in the §4.2 table (line 115) before it is explained in §6.4 (line 191). The §1 summary gives a short causal story, which does not satisfy the ‘chronology in the archive or compact’ clause.

expectations.text: B3 The H2 headings of the human zone, read alone, give the outline or the argument; question and decision headings carry their answer or ask
expectations.evidence: The H2s are bare topic labels: ‘1. 摘要与待决事项’, ‘2. 影响’, ‘3. 时间线’, ‘4. 根因与促成因素’, ‘5. 做得好的与靠运气的’, ‘6. 改进项与优先级建议’, ‘7. 待确认事项’, then three ‘附录’ headings. Read alone they give a generic postmortem table of contents, not the argument (no cause, no 105-minute / ~3,800-order impact, no 17-vs-10 person-day squeeze). The two decision-type headings (‘摘要与待决事项’, ‘改进项与优先级建议’) do not carry their ask or answer, e.g. the recommended plan.

expectations.text: C1 Conclusion first: the glance panel opens the document straight after the title and one metadata line, and its bottom line states the conclusion itself, not what the document covers
expectations.evidence: After the title and a compact metadata table (lines 3-10, plus a one-line no-blame note on line 12) the document goes straight into ‘## 1. 摘要与待决事项’ (line 14). It opens with the finding, not a description of the document: CFG-2231 changed the order-service pool limit 200 → 20, ‘本意只针对测试环境，却落在了全局默认值上’, pushed at 14:02 with no canary (line 16); then impact (line 18), why it took so long (line 20) and a decision box for 张伟 with a recommendation (lines 22-30). check_doc.py raised no C1 finding. expectations.text: C2 Compact panel: about 300 words of prose or fewer (tables and picture excluded; mechanical.json gives panel_words, where one Chinese character counts as 0.6 words), one line per decision and per risk, and verdict, decisions and top risks fit the first screen
expectations.evidence: mechanical.json stats.panel_words = 359 and Major C2 (line 14: the first section runs to about 359 words, budget 300). The decision is three multi-clause bullets (lines 26-28), not one line, and the panel lists no risks at all, so ‘one line per decision and per risk’ and ‘top risks fit the first screen’ are not met. The decision box itself does sit on the first screen (lines 22-30).

expectations.text: C3 Verdict, decisions and risks are complete and loud in the panel: the verdict has a glyph, confidence and basis; each decision has who, what, by when and a recommendation; at most 5 ranked risks, each with severity and consequence
expectations.evidence: The panel (lines 14-32) has no verdict line with a glyph, confidence level and basis. The decision (lines 22-30) gives who (张伟), what (which improvement items first) and a recommendation (方案一) but no ‘by when’ (only ‘下个迭代’ in the title). There is no ranked risk list with severity and consequence in the panel at all; the cost of deferring A2 appears only deep in §6.3 point 4 (line 185).

expectations.text: C4 Nothing invented: no verdict, decision or risk block without grounding in the sources, any ranking is traceable, empty slots are omitted
expectations.evidence: Every decision element is grounded: the options are built only from timeline.md's six items and the ~10 person-day budget (3+8+0.5+0.5+4+1 = 17; option 1 = 9; option 2 = 10, all re-computed and correct); the ranking rationale is stated (line 28, the cumulative table at lines 150-157, lines 180-185); the extra item A7 is labelled ‘候选’ with ‘没有负责人和估算’ (line 191) and rests on 李娜's chat line at 15:03; effect statements are labelled estimates (line 159). No verdict or risk block is fabricated and there are no empty slots. (The unlabelled no-blame sentence on line 12 is an addition but not a verdict, decision or risk.)

expectations.text: C5 Numbers in the panel trace to the sources (spot-check at least three); derived, merged or de-duplicated numbers say so
expectations.evidence: Spot-checks against timeline.md all match: 105 min (14:02-15:47), ~3,800 failed orders, ~1,200 users, availability 99.97% → 99.93% vs the 99.95% SLO, six items = 17 person-days, ~10 available (panel lines 16-28, ‘约’ preserved). Derived figures are signalled as sums or differences (‘合计 17 人天’, ‘缺 7 人天’, ‘共 9 人天，余 1 人天’, ‘合计只要 2 人天’). The 38 and 37 minute phase lengths are the writer's own intervals (14:20-14:58, 15:10-15:47); they are shown with their time ranges in §3.1 (lines 58-65) but are not flagged as derived inside the panel itself (minor weakness). expectations.text: D1 Diagram drawn: the eight related services (gateway, order-service, payment-service, inventory-service, user-service, notification-service, config-center, cache) and their call and push relationships are shown in at least one diagram

expectations.text: D5 D6 Explained and reproducible: alt text, a caption saying how to read the diagram and its takeaway, a legend where colour carries meaning, the relation stated (verbs on edges, or once when all edges are alike), the diagram source file beside each image, and an edge list or equivalent in the archive

expectations.text: E1 E2 Honesty: every judgment has a confidence level and its basis; content not in the inputs (assumptions, suggestions, inferences) is labelled as such; unknowns are listed

Labelling and unknowns are good: ‘假设“10 人天”是团队合计’ (line 141), ‘（推断，未验证）’ (line 127), ‘均为…估算，不是实测’ (line 159), ‘A7（候选）’ (line 191), † marks plus the Appendix B reconciliation, and §7 lists 7 unknowns with owners (lines 194-206). expectations.text: Root cause and factors right: CFG-2231 changed the order-service connection pool limit from 200 to 20 (meant for test only, applied to the global default); the config centre had no value-range validation; the push had no canary; the 5 s latency alert threshold was too lax; the runbook lacked a check of recent config changes; payment retries without backoff amplified the failure
expectations.evidence: §1 (line 16) and §3.2 (line 71): CFG-2231, merged 13:58, changed the order-service pool limit 200 → 20, ‘本意只改测试环境，却改到了全局默认值’. §4 and the §4.2 table (lines 97, 114-119) give: no value-range validation (plus no per-environment defaults, from the chat), push without canary (‘配置推送没有灰度’), 5 s alert threshold too lax (‘偏松’), runbook missing the ‘先查最近的配置变更’ step, and payment retries without backoff causing a retry storm (CPU 90%) that spreads the failure from order to payment (line 165). All consistent with timeline.md and the chat.

suggestions.assertion: D5 D6 Explained and reproducible: alt text, a caption saying how to read the diagram and its takeaway, a legend ..., the diagram source file beside each image, and an edge list or equivalent in the archive
suggestions.reason: Bundles six sub-conditions from two rules, so the verdict hinges on its weakest piece (here the caption takeaway and a labelled archive edge list). check_doc.py's D6 test also accepts only a same-stem source file, so it reports ‘no source file’ for all three PNGs although one make_figures.py in the same folder regenerates them, while the rubric text says ‘script file sits beside each image’. Align the checker and the rubric, and split D5 from D6.

suggestions.assertion: Raw chat log preserved: the chat excerpt is kept in the archive part or a linked file, not in the human zone, as the user asked
suggestions.reason: Passes for an open, uncollapsed 28-line block in a trailing appendix, the layout that A2 and A3 count as a defect, so it cannot tell an archive from a dump at the end of the page. State what counts (e.g. collapsed or in a sibling file under a labelled archive heading, not inline in the numbered sections) and keep the verbatim 28/28 check, which is solid.

No assertion scores whether the report surfaces the discrepancies and gaps in the fixtures: ‘~25 min wasted on the DB’ vs the chat timestamps (8 min), first response 14:12 vs 14:20, 14:52 thread dump vs 14:58 credit, the payment→order retry edge missing from services.csv, ‘no per-environment defaults’ appearing only in the chat, and the ‘10 person-days’ ambiguity. This run found and reconciled all of them (Appendix B, §7, the dashed edge), so a run that silently picked one source would score the same on content. Add an assertion that conflicts and gaps are named and say which source was used.

suggestions.assertion: C2 Compact panel: about 300 words of prose or fewer ...
suggestions.reason: ‘About 300’ is ambiguous next to the script's hard 300 limit: 359 words fails the checker but could be read as ‘about 300’. Give a number (e.g. at most 330) or defer to panel_words. Also, a panel with no risk lines is only caught indirectly through ‘one line per risk’.

suggestions.assertion: Decision for the tech lead: the panel asks Zhang Wei to prioritise the six follow-ups A1-A6, notes ... 17 person-days against about 10 available, and recommends which to do first
suggestions.reason: ‘Recommends which to do first’ would also pass a recommendation that overshoots the ~10 person-day budget. Require that the recommended set sums to at most 10 person-days (this run: 9) and that the deferred items are named; that is the real quality test of this decision.

suggestions.assertion: C1 Conclusion first: the glance panel opens the document straight after the title and one metadata line, and its bottom line states the conclusion itself ...
suggestions.reason: Passes for any report that starts with a summary paragraph. This run has no labelled bottom-line sentence (the first block is a causal narrative) and I credited it on judgement although the rule is Blocker-tier. State whether a one-sentence conclusion (root cause plus the ask) must be the first element.

eval_feedback.overall: The content assertions (root cause, impact, decision, raw log kept verbatim) are met by this no-skill baseline and mostly guard against regression rather than measure the skill. The format assertions discriminate, but several are bundled (D5 D6, E1 E2, A1) or depend on judgement calls (C1 bottom line, C2 ‘about’, raw-log ‘archive part’). The biggest gap is that nothing scores surfacing the source conflicts, which this run did well.
